title: Case E deploy-signal in boot-drain after full-team restart is ambiguous (honor vs skip)
ac: comprehension (#9184 hard gate): a fresh agent reading the modified event-mode-contract.md Case E deploy-signal section must derive (1) a deploy-signal in the boot drain is legitimate and must be HONORED (ack-stop deploy-halted + halt), not dismissed as residual restart telemetry — local references/ drift is NOT authoritative, the harness stored-checksum is; (2) you must NOT manually ack-cursor past it — that is the one path that can leave a genuinely-stale CLAUDE.md in place, and honoring is loop-free because the deploy sequence advances the cursor up front; (3) the finish-first nuance still holds — if boot resumed an in-progress task onto a feature branch, complete/hand off + return to main before honoring the halt.
method: Fresh agent (model: sonnet) given ONLY the modified event-mode-contract.md from branch squidsquad/task/13175, no other context. CQ spec authored + executed by verifier per #9184 (skill suggested the scenario in PR #13177; verifier owns the CQ).
target: references/sub-skills/common-events/event-mode-contract.md — Case E deploy-signal new boot-drain liveness sub-bullet + 2 traps (PR #13177, branch squidsquad/task/13175)

questions.q: During boot drain you fetch a deploy-signal targeting your alias; local clone shows no references/ drift and harness status is running. Correct action, and is it stale residual telemetry?
questions.expected: HONOR it (ack-stop deploy-halted, then halt) — do NOT dismiss as residual restart telemetry. Local 'no drift' does NOT prove CLAUDE.md is current (clone may be behind origin; pull-first deploy exists for this); the harness stored-checksum comparison is authoritative.
questions.must_not: Treating it as stale/residual and skipping; trusting the local references/ drift self-check; concluding status:running means no deploy needed.

questions.q: Could you just ack-cursor past it to stop the re-NUDGE instead of honoring? Why/why not, and the specific risk?
questions.expected: No. Honoring is loop-free (the deploy sequence advances your cursor past the signal up front; a no-op recompose is a clean idempotent success). A manual ack-cursor skip is the ONE path that can leave a genuinely-stale CLAUDE.md in place.
questions.must_not: Claiming ack-cursor-past is acceptable to stop re-waking; missing the stale-CLAUDE.md risk.

questions.q: If boot resumed an in-progress task onto a feature branch before you reached the deploy-signal, same action or different? What first?
questions.expected: Different — precondition (on main, clean tree) not met. Finish-first: complete and hand off (transition) the task, return to main, and only THEN emit ack-stop(deploy-halted) and halt.
questions.must_not: Honoring immediately while mid-task / on a feature branch; ignoring the on-main clean-tree precondition.

evidence: Fresh sonnet agent (id a5ba24e5a5693bd5e) given ONLY the branch's modified event-mode-contract.md, no other context. 3/3 correct, zero must_not violations. CQ1: 'honor it; do NOT dismiss as stale residual restart telemetry... harness stored-checksum comparison is authoritative.' CQ2: 'No... A manual ack-cursor skip is the one path that can leave a genuinely-stale CLAUDE.md in place... Honoring is loop-free.' CQ3: 'different... precondition not met... finish and hand off that task, return to main, and only then honor the deploy halt.' Contract premises independently verified against harness.py: cursor advanced up-front in deploy seq (L4646), ack-stop deploy-halted establishes intent=DEPLOYING synchronously on boot-drift path (L3252-3263), boot deploy-signal emitted on checksum drift.
